submitted.rationale: Index 11 (Bi 0.16, Cu 0.35, V 0.49) gave the highest measured photocurrent: 37.3 µA. That beat Bi-richer index 1 (28.5 µA) and Cu-richer index 57 (8.5 µA). The best region looks like a narrow optimum on the V-rich edge at moderate Cu.

rejected.reason: Measured 8.5 µA; photocurrent drops sharply at higher Cu and lower Bi
Not measured. Predicted gaps are small for CuO (0.20 eV) and Cu2O (1.56 eV, a p-type photocathode), and photocurrent already fell at Cu 0.43

consultations.verdict: Weakly against Cu-rich compositions: MEGNet HSE gap of CuO (mp-1692) is only 0.20 eV, so CuO-rich regions likely act as absorbing recombination sinks rather than photoanodes. That supports V-rich, Bi-containing compositions (BiVO4 ~2.4 eV, Cu vanadates ~2 eV) that absorb 2.72 eV photons. Index 1 is the most V-rich, Bi-rich candidate, so the model result supports it.

Mostly uninformative for index 11. Cu2O (mp-361) has a predicted HSE gap of 1.56 eV and is a p-type photocathode, not a photoanode. So the result argues against going to very Cu-rich compositions. Index 11 keeps V high (~0.49), trades Bi for Cu, and probes the Cu-vanadate + BiVO4 side of the high-V edge, which differs from index 1 (28.5 µA).

Mildly supportive. The predicted HSE gap of V2O5 (mp-25279) is 2.83 eV, so V-rich end members barely absorb 2.72 eV photons. Cu-vanadate mixtures (lower gap) should absorb better, which fits the measured increase from index 1 (28.5 µA) to index 11 (37.3 µA) as Bi fell and Cu rose. Index 57 continues that trend (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.43, V 0.46) while staying V-rich enough to avoid the CuO/Cu2O-dominated region flagged by the earlier gap results.
